subject: Observability add-ons: credits / SKU mapping for pilot and scale
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena@atlasai.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marco Chen <marco@atlasai.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Observability add-ons — pilot credits / SKU questions

Hi Mina,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — Atlas really liked the dashboard UX and the tracing sampling options. Before procurement spins up, procurement and engineering asked for a concise breakdown so we can map to our internal cost models. Can you confirm the following items and share a short written quote we can attach to our PO?

1) Retention buckets: you mentioned a 90-day and 365-day tier. For a 3-month pilot we expect ~120GB/day ingestion (~11M spans/day). What are the credit multipliers for 90d vs 365d?

2) Tracing: we need clarity on full-span retention vs sampled-span storage. Are there separate meter points (spans ingested vs spans retained) or a single aggregated metric?

3) Advanced dashboards: do seats (editors/viewers) map to per-user seat or to dashboard-view MAU? We have ~25 product users who will author dashboards and ~250 viewers.

4) Pilot concession: we prefer a 3-month pilot with credits and a one-time onboarding credit. Can you outline a pilot SKU that lets us run production traffic (not just PoC) and what limits would be in place?

5) Surge/egress: what charges apply for short bursts beyond pilot allocations? Any cap protections you can offer while we finalize a 12-month commit?

I've attached Atlas' procurement questionnaire and a short PO template so finance can move quickly once we have numbers. We need an internal review by Friday 10/23.

Thanks — looking forward to the sheet.

—Elena
Elena Ruiz
Head of Platform Engineering, Atlas AI
elena@atlasai.com

[attachment: Atlas_Security_Questionnaire.pdf]

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@atlasai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 13:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Observability add-ons — pilot credits / SKU questions

Hi Elena — great to hear Atlas found the demo helpful. Below is a compact mapping that I think will answer the procurement checklist. I'll follow up with a formal quote (and an editable pricing sheet) by EOD Wednesday.

Quick answers up front:
- Retention buckets: 90-day = base credits; 365-day = base * 2.8 (reflects storage + index cost). We can carve a pilot at 90-day with an option to snapshot-transfer to 365d at conversion rate above.
- Tracing meters: we produce two metered dimensions: spans_ingested and spans_retained. Billing is primarily on ingested spans; retained spans apply at the longer-term retention tier multiplier.
- Dashboards: two licenses — Author seat (editor) and Viewer seat. Viewer seat priced at 25% of Author. We also provide an MAU pass for high-volume read-only viewers as an alternative (recommended for >200 viewers).

Pilot SKU (recommended):
- 3 months, non-recurring credits
- Ingestion allowance: 3 months x 11M spans/day (we'll cap at 120GB/day equivalent)
- Retention: 90-day bucket included
- Dashboards: 5 Author seats + 200 Viewer MAU pass
- One-time onboarding + schema-mapping credit (8 hours of SE time)
- Pilot discount: 12% off list for the pilot term

Surge protection: we can add a temporary buffer (10% of ingestion allowance) for free during the pilot. Anything above the buffer will be billed at overage rates; we can negotiate a cap for the first 30 days of production in the event of unexpected traffic.

Attachments I will send with the quote: pricing_sheet_obs_addons_v2.xlsx (editable), pilot_term_sheet.pdf, and a suggested contract clause for capped surge protection. I'll include a sample invoice and the DocuSign link for easy acceptance.

Proposed next steps:
- I’ll send the formal quote + XLS by Wed 10/21 EOD PT.
- 30-minute call Thurs 10/22 to walk procurement through the PO and any redlines.

If that timeline works, I'll loop in legal for the capped surge language.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Sr. Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.ai

[attachment: pricing_sheet_obs_addons_v2.xlsx]

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@atlasai.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Oct 2026 08:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Observability add-ons — pilot credits / SKU questions

Elena / Mina — quick commercial notes from my side to make procurement's life easier:

1) If Atlas converts the pilot into a 12-month commit within 30 days of pilot end, we can apply a 9% conversion credit against the first year invoice (in addition to pilot discount).
2) For retention math: example numbers to include on the quote page so Atlas finance can model TCO:
   - Ingestion (11M spans/day) -> approx 330M spans/month -> base credits X/month
   - 90d retention multiplier = x1; 365d = x2.8 (as Mina said).
3) Dashboards: recommend the MAU pass vs per-viewer seat — it will be ~35% cheaper at your scale (250 viewers). We'll show both options on the sheet.
4) PO flow: we'll accept Atlas PO with standard SOW reference; attach pricing sheet and a one-line note: "Pilot credits are non-refundable; conversion credits apply if you sign a 12-month commitment."

I can prepare a single-page commercial summary to append to the PO. Mina — if legal flags the capped surge language, happy to trade a modest uplift to the pilot discount (e.g., 3% bump) in exchange for the cap.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai

From: Marco Chen <marco@atlasai.com>

Subject: Re: Observability add-ons — pilot credits / SKU questions

Mina / Ben — thanks for the rapid responses. A few clarifying items from procurement so we can circulate a tentative PO: 

- Please include line items for: ingestion credits (monthly), retention multiplier (explicit factor), dashboard author seats, viewer MAU pass, onboarding SE credit.
- Can you confirm the overage rate per 1M spans beyond the pilot buffer? Procurement prefers a per-unit overage number rather than a percentage.
- On the surge cap: Atlas legal asks for a mutual trigger clause (e.g., both sides must agree manual uncap for spikes >2x baseline). Is that acceptable?

If you can produce a one-page commercial summary + the priced XLS by EOD Monday 10/25, we can circulate internally and aim to sign the PO the following week. Attaching our PO template.

—Marco
Marco Chen
Senior Procurement Manager, Atlas AI
